The ideal gas model predicts and explains the behaviour of real gases in 
most practical situations. The key assumptions of this model are: 
* gas molecules are in constant random motion; 
» collisions between gas molecules are perfectly elastic; 
* the volume occupied by gas molecules is negligible compared with the 
volume of the container filled with the gas; 
* intermolecular forces between gas molecules are negligible; 
* average kinetic energy of gas molecules is directly proportional to 
absolute temperature (in kelvin).

The behaviour of ideal gases is described by three laws. 
Boyle's law: pressure of an ideal gas is inversely proportional to its volume 
at constant temperature (p o :—/) 
Charles’s law: volume of an ideal gas is directly proportional to its absolute 
temperature at constant pressure (V o T). 
Gay-Lussac’s law: pressure of an ideal gas is directly proportional to its 
absolute temperature at constant volume (p « T).
